ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR per-share figures are per ordinary share while the Nasdaq/NYSE price ($22.17) is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x0.5 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-24), Item 9 'The offer and listing' (p. 147): a two-for-one split of the outstanding ADSs effective December 3, 2012 'changed the ratio of our ADSs to shares from one ADS representing one share to two ADSs representing one share' — so one ADS represents one-half of an ordinary share (depositary: Bank of New York Mellon); the same 1/2 ratio is carried in the NYSE-registered ADS class title

capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — the engine's PPE capex tags carry no value from FY2020 onward in companyfacts (last filed FY2019: EUR 1,124,791,000 under PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentClassifiedAsInvestingActivities, per statements.json), while the filer's own cash-flow statement reports the combined PPE + capitalized-development-costs line every year. The override uses the latest filed year (FY2025, EUR 915M) for every missing period: it is 0.81x the last engine-filed value (in band), and it OVERSTATES capex for FY2023 (filed EUR 685M) and FY2024 (filed EUR 699M) by about 31-34%, so the median base OE/share it produces is conservative relative to a year-by-year filing-true base.
capex_override.source: Fresenius Medical Care consolidated statements of cash flows, investing activities: 'Purchases of property, plant and equipment and capitalized development costs' EUR 915M for FY2025 (Q4/FY2025 financial tables, February 24, 2026, reproducing the FY2025 Form 20-F cash-flow statement filed 2026-02-24); the same line is EUR 699M for FY2024 and EUR 685M for FY2023

moat_against: Reimbursement price-taker: U.S. Medicare/commercial rates are set by payors; FMS does not set its own price for its core treatment

Measured returns do not show a wide moat: ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) fell from 13.6% in 2018 to 4.6% in 2023 and 2024, recovering only to 7.2% in 2025; gross margin fell from 33.9% (2016) to 25.6% (2025)
U.S. same-market treatment growth was -0.9% in Q2 2026 — the core volume engine is flat, growth is rate/mix and Value-Based Care, not treatments

DaVita duopoly competition in the U.S. and labor-cost pressure across the clinic network; recurring special items (FME25+ program, portfolio optimization, China exit charge of about EUR 110M expected Q3 2026)
moat_for: World's largest dialysis provider: about 3,513 clinics treating about 290,000 patients (20-F FY2025, Item 4.B) — clinic density and purchasing scale no challenger can replicate quickly
Vertically integrated: Care Enablement makes the machines/dialyzers (incl. the 5008X, first FDA-cleared high-volume hemodiafiltration system in the U.S.) that Care Delivery clinics consume
Life-sustaining, non-discretionary recurring treatments; global dialysis population growing about 4-5%/yr (20-F Item 4.B) on diabetes/hypertension/obesity drivers
Value-Based Care scaling fast (segment revenue +28.2% in FY2025 to EUR 2,247M, segments.json) — a capitated-care position built on the clinic network and nephrologist relationships
moat_justification: World's leading dialysis provider (about 3,513 clinics, about 290,000 patients, 20-F Item 4.B) with vertical integration into machines/dialyzers (Care Enablement) and unmatched clinic scale — but a reimbursement price-taker in a DaVita duopoly, with ROIC proxy down from 13.6% (2018) to 4.6% (2023/24) recovering to 7.2% (2025) and gross margin down from 33.9% to 25.6%, so the measured franchise earns around its cost of capital, not well above it.
name: Fresenius Medical Care AG
one_liner: World's largest dialysis provider, moat 5/10 — clears 15% on the conservative override base ($3.23/ADS): weighted IRR 18.1%, IV@15 $27.88 vs $22.17, but the band runs C (bear 14.7%) to A (bull 22.0%) with net debt 3.55x normalized OE on the ADS basis, so size it to the bear end; clears 15% only below $27.88.

sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — no share-based compensation line is filed in the cash-flow statement / companyfacts for FY2020-2025 under any engine tag (statements.json: SBC blank FY2020-2025), so the engine's SBC leg is a gap even though Note 23 of the 20-F discloses the expense. Note 23's table (component sums, no total printed): total share-based compensation expense EUR 45,124,000 (FY2025) / EUR 38,458,000 (FY2024) / EUR 32,515,000 (FY2023), but the legacy plans (LTIP 2024+, LTIP 2022+, MB LTIP 2020, LTIP 2019, MB LTIP 2019) are cash-settled ('In cash') — a cash personnel cost already borne inside operating cash flow, not the non-cash addback the OE template subtracts — and only the new plans (LTIP 2025+, MB LTIP 2024+) can be equity-settled. The template's SBC leg is therefore the equity-settled expense: EUR 8,371,000 in FY2025, nil in FY2024/FY2023. EUR 10M flat is that figure rounded up and overstates FY2023/24 — conservative — and is about 0.5% of the gated years' owner's earnings, immaterial to the base and the tier either way; a sourced in-band estimate is used instead of the v4-style silent zero.
sbc_override.source: Anchor 1 (band): last engine-filed SBC value, FY2019 AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments EUR 1,992,000 (statements.json; filed FY2015-2019 range EUR 1,992,000-46,811,000) — EUR 10,000,000 is 5.02x that anchor, inside the 0.1x-10x band. Anchor 2 (filing economics): FY2025 Form 20-F Note 23 'Share-based plans' compensation-expense table — the EQUITY-settled allocations total EUR 8,371,000 in FY2025 (LTIP 2025+ EUR 6,293,000 + MB LTIP 2024+ EUR 2,078,000) and nil in FY2024/FY2023, so EUR 10M is that filing figure rounded up, applied flat

shares_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the engine has NO filed diluted share value to band against (last_filed_value is null) because companyfacts carries no diluted weighted-share series for this filer at all. The value is not an estimate — it is the weighted-average share count printed in the FY2025 20-F EPS presentation, verified in the filer's own reported statements.
shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted shares missing for FY2023/2024/2025 (in fact all years) in companyfacts; only the basic weighted-average count is tagged. The filer's own Note 22 reconciliation shows potentially dilutive shares are NIL in all three gated years (its legacy LTIPs are cash-settled virtual shares; see Note 23), so diluted EPS equals basic EPS on the filer's own presentation and the filed FY2025 weighted-average count IS the diluted denominator. The engine applies this single value to every missing period; the filed counts it replaces differ by less than 1% in the gated years (293,413,449 in FY2023/24 vs 291,190,575 in FY2025), so the 3-yr median base OE/share moves by under 1% from this flattening.
shares_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-24), Note 22 'Earnings per share' reconciliation of basic and diluted EPS: 'Weighted average number of shares outstanding' 291,190,575 for FY2025 (293,413,449 for FY2024 and FY2023), 'Potentially dilutive shares' shown as nil in all three years, basic EPS = diluted EPS (EUR 3.36 / 1.83 / 1.70, also identical on the face of the income statement); EDGAR companyfacts carries no diluted weighted-average series for any year (fundamentals.json warning: diluted share count not filed for 2016-2025)
